title: Hydrogen in transport in 2026
cover: Fewer stations, up to €19 a kilo and bets that are narrowing
Prepared 18 November 2026 · Astara Intelligence · Companion file: Hydrogen_Transport_InDepth_Data.xlsx

paras.how1: Scope: hydrogen as a fuel for road vehicles (cars, trucks and buses) and their refuelling stations. Hydrogen production appears only where it affects transport: public aid and manufacturers' electrolysers. Ships, trains, aviation, industry and stationary hydrogen are out of scope.
paras.how2: Marks: [EXT] is an external source, with its URL in Appendix B and in the Excel. [DB] is an entry in the AllMoving database, with its id and URL in the 12_Entries_DB sheet. [Own calculation] is arithmetic on figures that already carry a source.
paras.how3: Selection rule: a figure or fact is included only if the cited page was read. Nothing is estimated. "ND" means there is no defensible figure. What could not be checked is in Appendix C, not in the text.
paras.how4: Two caveats apply throughout: figures for different countries have different dates and definitions and are not added up; and a plan or a target is not a fact.
paras.sum1: In 2026 hydrogen in transport is narrowing: it grows in two markets and in the brands that keep betting on it, while the station network shrinks in Germany and Japan and the kilo reaches €19 in Germany.
paras.sum2: Sales of fuel cell cars rose in 2025 to 16,011 units, 24.4% more than in 2024, but according to SNE Research every market outside China and South Korea fell. In the first half of 2026, 4,643 were sold, 13% more than a year earlier, with Hyundai at 3,337 (+161.9%) and Toyota at 306 (-56.7%) [EXT: SNE Research via electrive and Asia Business Daily].
paras.sum3: The network is shrinking in Germany and Japan. Germany has about 50 public stations open in January 2026, against more than 80 two years earlier [EXT: electrive.net]. Japan counts 149 [EXT: Nikkei via Automotive World]. In California, 50 are open and 11 are out of service, with average availability close to 60% [EXT: California Energy Commission]. Refuelling costs up to about €19 a kilo in Germany [EXT: autohaus.de].
paras.sum4: GM and its joint venture with Honda are leaving, and the projects with public money remain. GM ended development of next-generation fuel cells and its joint venture with Honda will stop producing before the end of 2026; Arthur Bus and Quantron went insolvent. Hyundai, BMW and Toyota carry on, along with the European truck alliance, €220m of German aid and the European Hydrogen Bank, while Daimler's series production of trucks is postponed from 2027 to the 2030s [EXT: electrive, gasworld, Daimler Truck].
paras.s1_h: Cars: growth in just two markets
paras.s1p1: 16,011 fuel cell cars were sold worldwide in 2025, 24.4% more than in 2024 [EXT: SNE Research via electrive, 23 February 2026]. By market: China 7,797 (the source calls the figure "commercial"), South Korea 6,802, Europe 566, Japan 430 and North America 365. According to the same source, every market outside China and South Korea fell.
paras.s1p2: By brand, Hyundai sold 6,861 (+78.9%, with the second-generation Nexo) and Toyota 1,168 (-39.1%). In Japan, Nikkei counts 431 sales in 2025, 83% fewer than in 2021 [EXT: Nikkei via Automotive World].
paras.s1p3: In the first half of 2026, 4,643 units were sold worldwide against 4,110 a year earlier (+13%). Hyundai sold 3,337 (+161.9%), Toyota 306 (-56.7%) and Chinese commercial vehicles 921 (-54.4%) [EXT: SNE Research via Asia Business Daily, 6 August 2026].
paras.s1p4: The new Nexo costs from €69,900 in Germany (the previous one, from €77,290), with 826 km of range and a hydrogen consumption of 0.8 to 0.9 kg per 100 km [EXT: ecomento.de, 8 January 2026]. BMW will launch the iX5 Hydrogen in 2028, with €273m of public aid from the federal government and Bavaria; the 750 km range is a target [DB + EXT: electrive, 11 September 2026].
paras.s2p1: Interact Analysis counted 1,369 hydrogen stations deployed worldwide at the end of 2024: 849 in Asia-Pacific (62%), 412 in Europe, the Middle East and Africa and 108 in the Americas. China, South Korea, Japan, France and Germany account for 79% [EXT: Interact Analysis via EV Candi, 7 February 2025]. It is a single-source count: there is no worldwide count for 2026.
paras.s2p2: The 2026 country figures show a network that is shrinking or not taking off:
paras.s2b1: Germany: about 50 public stations open in January 2026 (13 with 700 bar only, 35 with both pressures and 2 with 350 bar only); two years earlier there were more than 80 [EXT: electrive.net, 15 January 2026].
paras.s2b2: Japan: 149 stations in February 2026, 10% fewer than five years ago and less than half the 320 the government had planned [EXT: Nikkei via Automotive World].
paras.s2b3: California: 50 stations open to the public on 2 September 2025 and 11 temporarily out of service. Average network availability over the last year was close to 60%. There are 14,128 fuel cell cars registered (April 2025) [EXT: California Energy Commission].
paras.s2b4: China: 574 stations and more than 360 t/day of capacity at the end of 2025; an official cited more than 590 in June 2026 [EXT: China Daily, 23 March 2026].
paras.s2p3: Element 2, which was building stations in the United Kingdom, had a winding-up petition served in September 2026; the article does not confirm the liquidation [DB + EXT: gasworld, 3 November 2026].
paras.s3p1: In Germany hydrogen costs up to about €19/kg at the pump (gross price, January 2026); prices are dynamic and vary by region and pressure [EXT: autohaus.de, 13 January 2026]. H2 Mobility has cut the price by about 10% at 5 stations (1 June) and by 12 to 16% at 15 stations (1 October); none of the sources read gives the absolute price before and after [DB + EXT: electrive.net, 28 September 2026]. For trucks, the hylane tariff at H2 Mobility stations is about €8/kg net from 1 January 2026, only with its card and for contracted volumes [EXT: solarserver.de, 18 November 2025].
paras.s3p2: Own calculation: with a consumption of 0.8 to 0.9 kg per 100 km and the maximum price of €19/kg, a car spends €15 to 17 on hydrogen per 100 km. It is a ceiling: at stations with a price cut it would be somewhat less. There is no verified electricity price, so it is not compared with a battery-electric car.
paras.s3p3: In China the kilo costs 35 to 76 yuan in the pilot cities and the target of three ministries is to get below 25 yuan in 2030 [EXT: China Daily, 23 March 2026]. It is not converted to euros.
paras.s3p4: The US Department of Energy's goals (May 2024 plan) are USD 2/kg for production in 2026 and USD 1/kg in 2031, USD 7/kg for hydrogen dispensed to heavy-duty vehicles in 2028 and USD 80/kW for the heavy-transport fuel cell system in 2030. They are goals, not actual costs; the DOE site warns that a new plan is coming [EXT: US Department of Energy].
paras.s4_h: Trucks: series production slips, pilots continue
paras.s4p1: Daimler Truck says its customers have driven almost 600,000 km with fuel cell trucks and plans to deploy a small series of 100 next-generation fuel cell trucks with customers from the end of 2026. It is a plan, not deliveries. electrive recalls that Daimler delayed series production from 2027 to the 2030s [EXT: Daimler Truck, 15 September 2026; electrive, 3 September 2026].
paras.s4p2: On 15 September 2026 Daimler, Volvo, Toyota, Bosch, Air Liquide, TotalEnergies, TEAL Mobility and MB Energy announced cooperation on hydrogen mobility in Europe, with a horizon of 2030. Daimler is also preparing hydrogen combustion engine trucks, which according to the release would come out "next year" [EXT: Daimler Truck].
paras.s4p3: The Rhenus pilot with Daimler GenH2 trucks on liquid hydrogen measures a consumption of 5.6 to 8.0 kg per 100 km and adds up to about 225,000 km in phase 1 (5 trucks). Phase 2 has five customers. According to the source, there are only two liquid hydrogen stations in Germany [DB + EXT: electrive, 26 March 2026].
paras.s4p4: The German government has put €220m of aid into the hydrogen truck network; more than 70 stations and 800 trucks were applied for, with more than 500 applications in the first call, which would be decided in the second half of 2026 [DB + EXT: electrive, 3 September 2026]. Thailand approved 1,490 million baht (about €39m) to produce the Toyota Hilux FCEV from December 2027, up to 3,000 units a year [DB + EXT: electrive, 27 October 2026].
paras.s4p5: Quantron became insolvent at the end of October 2024, its founder bought the assets on 1 April 2025 and in September 2026 Quantron and HyperView set up a joint venture in China, with Foxconn as manufacturer. It expects 100 pre-series vehicles at the end of 2026: this is a plan [DB + EXT: electrive, 18 September 2026].
paras.s5p1: The US Fuel Cell and Hydrogen Energy Association (FCHEA, an industry source) reports small and growing fleets: SamTrans has 10 buses in service and 108 more approved; Victor Valley presented 13 earlier in 2026; Montebello put 3 into operation in August 2026; New York's MTA received 2 in June 2026 and its future Gun Hill station could serve 40; Rochester RTS has 2 and will acquire 10 more. Three New York agencies receive USD 52.5m from the Zero-Emission Transit Transition programme (October 2025). The source itself says operation is concentrated in pilots and relatively small fleets [EXT: FCHEA, August 2026].
paras.s5p2: In Europe, Arthur Bus (Poland) filed for insolvency on 26 November 2025, affecting 20 buses ordered by Lublin and 3 by Buspunkt [DB + EXT: electrive, 3 February 2026].
paras.s6p1: Exits and insolvencies. In October 2025 GM ended development of next-generation fuel cells and cancelled a USD 55m plant in Detroit; it had invested almost USD 3,000m since the late nineties [EXT: CBT News, 13 October 2025]. Its joint venture with Honda (FCSM) will stop producing before the end of 2026 [EXT: Automotive Manufacturing Solutions, 22 January 2026]. To these are added Arthur Bus, Quantron and Element 2.
paras.s6p2: Bets and aid. In November 2026 Hyundai unveiled its first 5 MW PEM electrolyser, with series production in 2027, and signed a non-binding agreement with Air Liquide on hydrogen mobility in China [DB + EXT: gasworld, 4 and 9 November 2026]. In the third auction the European Hydrogen Bank signed €62m for Gen2 Energy (Norway, €3.48/kg for ten years) and €139.8m for Hy2gen (Denmark, €0.97/kg for ten years) [DB + EXT: gasworld, 11 and 16 November 2026].
paras.s7p1: China's target is 100,000 fuel cell vehicles in 2030; the five pilot city clusters had sold 39,023 [EXT: China Daily, 23 March 2026]. In the first half of 2026 sales were 550 according to CAAM (-63.5%) and 921 commercial vehicles according to SNE Research (-54.4%): they use different definitions. In the fourth quarter of 2025 more than 3,000 units a month were exceeded [EXT: SMM with data from CAAM, 17 July 2026].

C: Coverage of the AllMoving database. The "Hydrogen & Fuel Cell Mobility" line (id 96) has 799 entries: 216 from 2020, 264 from 2021, 124 from 2022, 59 from 2023, 70 from 2024, 19 from 2025 and 25 from 2026. It measures what was ingested, not market activity: it is not read as a trend. Of the 25 from 2026, the ones that state a fact were read and used (12 entries in all, with those from 2025); the rest are known only by their headline and are not used. Check: Before printing, do not show the volume per year as a trend.

Global market data (committed investment, production capacity, number of projects, demand). The IEA, Hydrogen Council and S&P Global pages, the ICCT PDF on Hainan and the California Energy Commission PDF block automated reading. Figures confirmed only in the trade press have been left out of this document. Check: For a global market overview, those original reports must be read.

Worldwide station count. The figure of 1,369 at the end of 2024 is from Interact Analysis, cited by EV Candi. Other counts give different figures and could not be read. There is no worldwide count for 2026. Check: Always cite "Interact Analysis, end of 2024".

Different dates and definitions across countries. Germany counts public stations (January 2026), Japan stations (February 2026), California stations open to the public (September 2025) and China stations (December 2025). They are not added up or compared on one axis. Check: The design must show the date and the definition on every bar.

China sales. The CAAM count gives 550 for the first half of 2026 and SNE Research 921 commercial vehicles. They use different definitions. The Chinese figure for 2025 (7,797) appears as "commercial" in the source. Check: Do not speak of "cars" in China without making this clear.

Prices. They are dynamic and vary by region and pressure. There is no absolute price before and after the H2 Mobility cuts. Yuan are not converted to euros. There is no verified electricity price, so the cost per 100 km is not compared with that of a battery-electric car. Check: Do not add comparisons with electric cars without a separate source.

2026 sources. Most are trade press (electrive, gasworld, Automotive World, Hydrogen Fuel News), not releases or official reports. Sensitive cases: Element 2 (the article does not confirm the liquidation) and Arthur Bus (financial data from second-hand Polish press). Check: Re-read the Element 2 and Arthur Bus sources before printing.

Plans and targets. Daimler's 100 trucks, the Hilux FCEV, the BMW iX5 Hydrogen, the DOE goals and China's targets are plans or targets, not facts. The DOE site warns that it will replace its 2024 plan. Check: Label them "plan" or "target" in the design.
Industry source. The US bus data come from FCHEA, the sector association. Check: Cite it as an industry source.

What was left out on purpose. Every figure that could not be read at the source has been removed, along with those from search-engine summaries, from opinion pieces, company claims that were not checked (for example the truck specifications announced by Chinese manufacturers) and calculations that mixed bases from different sources. Check: The detail of what was removed is in RETIRADO.md in the folder, for the editor.

Database entries with low classification confidence. Three 2026 entries of line 96 (a production hub in Asturias, RINA Morocco and Hyundai's European vision) have a doubtful classification. They are not used. Check: Pass them to the Classification and upload chat for review.
